transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess the main thing that finally made me come in is my eating. It’s been really up and down. Some weeks I barely want dinner at all, and then other nights I’m standing in the kitchen after everyone’s asleep eating crackers and sweets. It just feels kind of out of control.
After times when you feel like you've eaten a lot or lost control, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or exercise a lot to try to balance it out?

No, I don’t do that. I don’t make myself throw up or take laxatives. And I wouldn’t say I exercise to make up for it either. I usually just feel bad about it afterward and try to eat less the next day, but nothing like that.
How often do you feel like you lose control and eat a lot in one sitting, and have you noticed any pattern in when these episodes happen?

It’s not every day, but it comes in spells. Some weeks I’m hardly eating much at dinner, and then other nights I’ll end up in the kitchen after everyone’s gone to bed, eating crackers or sweets and feeling like I’m not really stopping when I meant to. The pattern seems to be more at night, when it’s quiet and I’m by myself.
Do these episodes of eating late at night happen when you're feeling stressed, anxious, or down, or do they seem to happen more randomly?

It doesn’t feel totally random, no. It’s more like my eating is just all over the place. Some weeks I barely touch dinner, and then other nights, after everyone’s gone to bed, I’ll be standing in the kitchen eating crackers or sweets. I don’t always know what sets it off, but the late-night part is definitely when it tends to happen.
When you find yourself eating during these late-night episodes, do you notice that you're eating much more quickly than normal or feel like you can't stop once you start?

Yeah, sometimes it feels like once I’m there eating, I don’t really stop when I meant to. I wouldn’t say I’m always eating super fast, but I’ll be standing there having crackers or sweets, and then it’s more than I planned. That’s part of what pushed me to come in—my eating just feels all over the place.
When you're in the kitchen late at night eating, do you feel like you can't stop or control how much you eat once you start?

Yeah… I think so, at least sometimes. I’ll go in thinking I’ll just have a little something, and then I’m standing there eating crackers or sweets after everyone’s gone to bed, and it ends up being more than I meant to. It’s part of why I came in—my eating just feels really all over the place.
Has this pattern of eating affected your daily life, like causing you distress, affecting your relationships, or making it hard to focus on work or other activities?

Yes, it has. It’s been causing me stress, and I feel like I’ve fallen behind on things I’m supposed to be doing, like my facilitator training and work on my private blog. My projects and even explaining things have gotten harder to organize.

And at home, there’s been more tension, so it’s harder to keep normal routines with my husband. It’s not completely taking over everything, but it is affecting my day-to-day life.
Do you judge yourself or feel bad about your body shape or weight after these eating episodes?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think I focus much on my body shape or weight right after. I might feel annoyed with myself for eating when I didn’t plan to, but I haven’t really noticed it being about how I look.
Do you feel a lot of distress or upset specifically about these late-night eating episodes, like feeling ashamed or really frustrated with yourself afterward?

Yeah, I do get upset about it. I wouldn’t say it’s always shame exactly, but it’s frustrating. What really pushed me to come in is that my eating feels so all over the place—some weeks I barely eat dinner, and then other nights I’m in the kitchen after everyone’s asleep eating crackers or sweets. Afterward I just feel like, “Why did I do that again?”
When you feel upset or frustrated after these late-night eating episodes, is it because you're worried about your weight or the way your body looks?
Not really, no. I don’t think it’s mostly about my weight or how I look. It’s more that I feel irritated with myself, like I didn’t have control over it or I got off track again.
Do you usually feel hungry when you find yourself eating late at night, or do you sometimes eat even when you’re not really hungry?

Sometimes I’m hungry, but not always. That’s part of what’s been bothering me—my eating is just all over the place. Some weeks I barely touch dinner, and then other nights I’m standing in the kitchen after everyone’s gone to bed eating crackers or sweets, even if I’m not really sure I’m hungry.
When you’re in the kitchen late at night eating, are you fully awake and aware of what you’re doing, or does it ever feel like you’re on autopilot or not fully in control of your actions?

I think I’m awake and aware. It doesn’t feel like sleepwalking or anything like that. It’s more like I end up there, knowing what I’m doing, eating crackers or sweets after everyone’s gone to bed, and then I feel frustrated because my eating has been so all over the place.

Outside of these late-night eating episodes, do you ever find yourself eating much more rapidly than normal, eating until you're uncomfortably full, or eating large amounts when you're not actually hungry?

I don’t know if it’s exactly eating really fast or until I’m painfully full. It’s more that my appetite is all over the place. Some weeks I barely eat dinner, and then other nights I’m in the kitchen late eating crackers or sweets after everyone’s gone to bed, even when I’m not sure I’m actually hungry.
Is there ever a time when you eat a very large amount of food in just a short period, like within a couple of hours, not just grazing throughout the night?

Not really like a huge amount all at once, no. It’s more uneven than that—some weeks I barely eat dinner, and then other nights I’ll end up in the kitchen after everyone’s asleep eating crackers or sweets. It feels out of control in a frustrating way, but more like picking at things or snacking than one big binge in a couple hours.
When you're eating during these late-night episodes, do you feel like you're not in control of your eating — like you can't stop even if you want to?

Yeah, it does feel hard to stop sometimes. I’m aware of what I’m doing, but I’ll be standing there after everyone’s gone to bed eating crackers or sweets, and part of me is thinking I should just go back to bed. My eating has just been really all over the place—some weeks I barely touch dinner, and then other nights it’s like this.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy around the same time these eating patterns started?

Yeah, I have. Around those times, I get these stretches where everything in the house just feels gray and heavy. I’ll end up sitting at the kitchen table feeling really empty, even when nothing bad actually happened that day.
Have you had days where you feel down or hopeless nearly every day, or where you can't enjoy things you used to like, and if so, how often does that happen?

Yes. I do get stretches like that where I feel down most days. The house just feels gray and heavy, and I’ll sit at the kitchen table feeling empty, even if nothing really bad happened that day. I wouldn’t say it’s every single day all the time, but when it comes on, it can be pretty frequent.

There is no evidence of significant concern about body shape or weight, which makes bulimia nervosa (F50.0) unlikely.
